name: Behavioral and Neural Measures of Auditory Distraction in Participants with Tinnitus
description: In this exploratory study, we tested whether tinnitus burden, assessed using the Tinnitus Handicap Inventory (THI), was associated with behavioral and neural responses to external auditory distraction. Thirty adults with chronic tinnitus completed behavioral and electroencephalographic (EEG) testing. Participants with lower and higher THI scores were similar in age and hearing thresholds. Data from twenty-three neurotypical adults provided an additional reference cohort. Participants classified sequences of amplitude-modulated tones as random or repeating during behavioral testing or combined behavioral and EEG recording sessions. Competing noise or melodic distractors imposed lower and higher levels of distraction, respectively. Melodic distractors reduced response accuracy more than noise distractors, with comparable effects in the lower and higher THI groups. Neural synchronization to changes in the target sequence also de-creased more with melodic distractors, but this effect did not differ between groups. Other measures of synchronization to target and distractor features showed no significant group differences. Descriptions of data headers can be found in the included README document. Figure numbers refer to the manuscript reporting these results, available as a preprint at https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.01.27.702073
